rationale:
`ValidationContext.graph` has two obligations: it borrows the application domain, and direct calls on that domain bypass dependency tracking.

1. **Borrow the domain.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]` asserts `std::ptr::eq(inspection.graph(), &graph)`. This shows the returned reference is the same domain the context was built with, not a copy or a different object. It also uses `inspection.graph().cache()` in later reads, which only compiles because the reference is a usable `&D`.

2. **Direct calls bypass tracking.** The same test calls `inspection.graph().node_content(...)` directly. It then asserts `inspection.dependencies().is_empty()`, so the direct read recorded no dependency. Tracked reads made later through `read` and `read_snapshot` do record dependencies. That contrast shows the bypass is specific to calls made on the borrowed domain. An implementation that tracked reads made through `graph()` would fail this assertion.

3. **Signature.** The `&'d D` signature is covered by compilation of the test and by the public API check in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`. That check is marked as a test of `requirements.sdk.public-api.exports` and `requirements.sdk.public_api`, not of this requirement. It adds nothing to the two behavioural obligations above.

The test carries a `{test}` reference to this requirement, so there is no marking gap. I found no further obligations or boundaries in the text.

text: Borrow the application domain. Calls made directly on the domain bypass the context’s dependency tracking.
